title: PNP tightens ASEAN Summit security following tensions at protests
summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Tuesday said tighter security measures will be implemented for the Association of Southeast Asia Nations (ASEAN) Summit 2026 due to tensions during recent…

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Tuesday said tighter security measures will be implemented for the Association of Southeast Asia Nations (ASEAN) Summit 2026 due to tensions during recent protests.

PNP chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. ordered commanders to address identified security vulnerabilities, strengthen intelligence-sharing, and ensure that all security units remain prepared for the remaining summit activities.

"We cannot afford complacency when the security and credibility of our country are at stake. I have directed all commanders to close security gaps without delay, and keep our forces fully coordinated," he said in a statement.
"The success of the ASEAN Summit rests not only on our ability to prevent threats but also on our capability to protect people while upholding their rights," he added.
Some 23,000 government personnel, comprised of about 20,000 cops and 3,000 force multipliers, have been deployed to secure the 49th ASEAN Summit, the PNP said.
The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO), Police Regional Offices 3 and 4A, and Camp Crame-based units have also been placed under full alert status from November 13 to 19.
President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. has directed to maintain a safe, peaceful, and orderly environment throughout the summit, according to the PNP.
Nartatez said the police force would remain vigilant and professional while respecting the rights of the public.
"A successful summit must be measured not only by the security of our guests but also by the safety and dignity of our people," he said.
Over 200 protesters were arrested in Sucat, Muntinlupa during a protest caravan and were brought to Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City as ASEAN Summit 2026 opened on Sunday. — VDV, GMA News
